title: Whole-blob upsert has no compare-and-swap: a delayed/flaky-network write can silently roll back a newer, already-"saved" edit from another device, with no backup to recover it
where: saveToSupabase() index.html:1324-1344; sync poll ordering check index.html:2551-2564; MAX_BLOB_BYTES/backup guard index.html:2454-2487
detail: saveToSupabase() computes `updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` on the CLIENT before the network call, then does `.upsert({user_id, data, updated_at}, {onConflict:'user_id'})` with no WHERE/version guard (confirmed: no trigger or check constraint on user_data.updated_at in supabase/migrations/000_core.sql — it's a plain `default now()` column, never conditioned on in the upsert). Whichever request physically reaches Postgres LAST wins outright and overwrites both `data` and `updated_at`, regardless of which edit happened later in real time or what timestamp value it carries. The client-side ordering guard at index.html:2557 (`row.updatedAt > lastSeenAt.current`) only protects the LOCAL in-memory comparison on the polling device; it does nothing to stop the DB row itself from being overwritten by an out-of-order or clock-skewed write from another device.
failure: Nurse edits a shift on her phone at a hospital with spotty WiFi (edit at real time T0); the save request is delayed in flight. Seconds later she edits the same data on her laptop at home over a good connection (edit at T1>T0); that save completes immediately and succeeds — clearing the laptop's own local backup (index.html:2475) because its save succeeded. If the phone's delayed request then arrives at Supabase after the laptop's, the row is overwritten with the phone's STALE data and an OLDER `updated_at`. The laptop's newer edits are now gone from the cloud. Because they were never in `writeBackup()` (that only fires when a save FAILS, and the laptop's save reported success), there is no copy anywhere to recover them once the laptop's tab is closed or its browser data cleared — reopening the app anywhere else (or signing in on a new device) hydrates the phone's older data. The laptop's own 15s poll never flags this either, because the phone's `updated_at` is chronologically earlier than the laptop's `lastSeenAt`, so `row.updatedAt > lastSeenAt.current` is false and the discrepancy is never even surfaced.
fix: Add an optimistic-concurrency guard to the upsert (e.g. pass the last-seen `updated_at` and use `.eq('updated_at', lastSeenAt)` with an update, falling back to insert/upsert only when no row exists yet), or move to a monotonic version column with a DB-side check so a stale write is rejected (surfacing a conflict to the user/backup path) instead of silently winning. This does not require full versioned ops (PR #67's scope) — just enough to stop a slower write from clobbering a faster one.
